references.title: Charge-Informed Quantum Error Correction
references.authors: Vlad Temkin, Zack Weinstein, Ruihua Fan, Daniel Podolsky, Ehud Altman
references.summary: Develops optimal and minimum-cost-flow decoders for U(1) symmetry-enriched topological memories when local anyon charges are measurable, and finds a substantial advantage over charge-agnostic decoding.
references.project_relevance: The closest established precedent for using symmetry-resolved anyon data to raise a decoding threshold; our SU(2) proposal replaces scalar charge labels with representation and fusion-channel information.

references.title: Strong-to-Weak Symmetry Breaking in Open Quantum Systems: From Discrete Particles to Continuum Hydrodynamics
references.authors: Jacob Hauser, Kaixiang Su, Hyunsoo Ha, Jerome Lloyd, Thomas G. Kiely, Romain Vasseur, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, Cenke Xu, Matthew P. A. Fisher
references.summary: Relates U(1) strong-to-weak symmetry breaking to the loss of inferability of discrete particle worldlines and constructs explicit decoding protocols in one and two dimensions.
references.project_relevance: Provides an important comparison point: it formulates decoding through worldline inferability, whereas this project deliberately tests a more practical snapshot decoder that uses only the currently measured endpoint and herald fields.

references.title: Strong-to-Weak Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking in Mixed Quantum States
references.authors: Leonardo A. Lessa, Ruochen Ma, Jian-Hao Zhang, Zhen Bi, Meng Cheng, Chong Wang
references.summary: Introduces robust diagnostics for strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking in mixed states and identifies a decohered Ising transition as the ungauged counterpart of toric-code decodability.
references.project_relevance: Supplies the symmetry language connecting decoder failure to a mixed-state information transition.

references.title: Diagnostics of Mixed-State Topological Order and Breakdown of Quantum Memory
references.authors: Ruihua Fan, Yimu Bao, Ehud Altman, Ashvin Vishwanath
references.summary: Characterizes the breakdown of topological quantum memory using intrinsic mixed-state information measures and connects their transition to the optimal toric-code decoding threshold.
references.project_relevance: Gives the baseline information-theoretic meaning of the threshold that a herald-aware decoder should be compared against.

references.title: Symmetry Enforced Entanglement in Maximally Mixed States
references.authors: Amin Moharramipour, Leonardo A. Lessa, Chong Wang, Timothy H. Hsieh, Subhayan Sahu
references.summary: Shows that strong non-Abelian symmetries such as SU(2) can enforce long-range mixed-state entanglement, unlike Abelian symmetry sectors.
references.project_relevance: Explains why the SU(2) extension is not a cosmetic enlargement of the U(1) charge-informed model.

references.title: String Order Parameters for Symmetry Fractionalization in an Enriched Toric Code
references.authors: José Garre-Rubio, Mohsin Iqbal, David T. Stephen
references.summary: Constructs an enriched toric-code model and uses string order parameters to diagnose symmetry fractionalization carried by anyons.
references.project_relevance: Provides concrete symmetry-enriched topological-order language for assigning additional representation data to toric-code excitations.

references.title: Topological Quantum Memory
references.authors: Eric Dennis, Alexei Kitaev, Andrew Landahl, John Preskill
references.summary: Foundational analysis of topological quantum memory, its statistical-mechanical mapping, error thresholds, and matching-based decoding.
references.project_relevance: Defines the endpoint-only toric/surface-code baseline and the standard hidden-string decoding problem.

references.title: Optimal Circuit-Level Decoding for Surface Codes
references.authors: Bettina Heim, Krysta M. Svore, Matthew B. Hastings
references.summary: Compares minimum-weight perfect matching with optimal maximum-likelihood decoding under circuit-level surface-code noise.
references.project_relevance: Helps separate gains from extra herald information from gains available merely by replacing MWPM with a more optimal decoder.

references.title: Improved Decoding of Circuit Noise and Fragile Boundaries of Tailored Surface Codes
references.authors: Oscar Higgott, Thomas C. Bohdanowicz, Aleksander Kubica, Steven T. Flammia, Earl T. Campbell
references.summary: Introduces belief-matching and belief-find: belief propagation first estimates correlated fault probabilities, then matching or union-find turns those beliefs into a correction.
references.project_relevance: The closest off-the-shelf architecture for turning herald-conditioned edge beliefs into a weighted matching problem. Its factor-graph front end can be adapted to include a vertex likelihood for the herald observation.

references.title: Improved Quantum Error Correction Using Soft Information
references.authors: Christopher A. Pattison, Michael E. Beverland, Marcus P. da Silva, Nicolas Delfosse
references.summary: Derives soft-information versions of MWPM and union-find that use likelihoods retained from noisy measurements instead of immediately hardening them to binary outcomes.
references.project_relevance: Provides a principled precedent for converting an auxiliary noisy readout into decoder weights rather than consuming it with deterministic local correction rules.

references.title: Linear-Time Maximum Likelihood Decoding of Surface Codes over the Quantum Erasure Channel
references.authors: Nicolas Delfosse, Gilles Zémor
references.summary: Gives a linear-time maximum-likelihood surface-code decoder when the locations of erased qubits are known.
references.project_relevance: Defines the clean erasure-information limit against which herald information should be compared, while also clarifying that a vertex herald is not itself a known erased edge.

references.title: Breadth-First Graph Traversal Union-Find Decoder
references.authors: Matthias C. Löbl, Susan X. Chen, Stefano Paesani, Anders S. Sørensen
references.summary: Develops breadth-first Tanner-graph variants of union-find that jointly handle Pauli errors and qubit erasures for topological and qLDPC codes.
references.project_relevance: Offers an efficient alternative back end if herald evidence can be converted into edge erasure probabilities or seeded cluster growth; the associated official implementation is archived separately.

references.title: Efficient Algorithms for Maximum Likelihood Decoding in the Surface Code
references.authors: Sergey Bravyi, Martin Suchara, Alexander Vargo
references.summary: Presents exact maximum-likelihood decoding for a special independent-noise model and an approximate tensor-network decoder for more general surface-code noise.
references.project_relevance: Supplies the natural small-system oracle for checking whether a herald-aware approximate decoder is actually approaching the posterior optimum.

references.title: Belief-Matching Decoder
references.authors: Oscar Higgott and contributors
references.summary: Official Python implementation of belief-matching using ldpc belief propagation and PyMatching as the MWPM subroutine.
references.project_relevance: Primary implementation reference for the proposed belief-propagation-to-reweighted-MWPM decoder path in Lab 001.

references.title: Union-Find Decoder
references.authors: NBI Hybrid Quantum Networks group
references.summary: Official C/Python implementation of the breadth-first union-find decoder, including surface-code examples with both Pauli errors and erasures.
references.project_relevance: Executable reference for testing whether herald-derived soft erasures can profitably seed a union-find decoder.

references.title: Relay-BP Decoder
references.authors: Thomas Alexander, Tristan Müller, and contributors
references.summary: Rust implementation of Relay-BP for qLDPC codes with Python bindings, Stim/Sinter integration, and tests for bivariate-bicycle and rotated-surface-code workflows.
references.project_relevance: Implementation reference for studying a relay-style belief-propagation front end; it is not a drop-in implementation of the project's syndrome–herald factor model.

references.title: Improved Belief Propagation Is Sufficient for Real-Time Decoding of Quantum Memory
references.authors: Tristan Müller, Thomas Alexander, Michael E. Beverland, Markus Bühler, Blake R. Johnson, Thilo Maurer, Drew Vandeth
references.summary: Introduces Relay-BP, a qLDPC heuristic that chains belief-propagation runs with disordered memory strengths to mitigate oscillations and trapping sets under circuit noise.
references.project_relevance: A high-value BP-family comparison for scalable qLDPC decoding and hardware-aware message passing; adapting it to the project's herald observation would require a new matched factor graph and validation.

references.title: LieART 2.0 — A Mathematica Application for Lie Algebras and Representation Theory
references.authors: Robert Feger, Thomas W. Kephart, Robert J. Saskowski
references.summary: Presents LieART 2.0, a Mathematica application for root and weight systems, irreducible-representation properties, tensor-product decompositions, and subalgebra branching rules; its expanded tables cover classical and exceptional algebras through rank 15.
references.project_relevance: A computational reference for making SU(2) and SU(N) representation labels, tensor-product channels, and branching conventions explicit before using non-Abelian side information in the decoder model.

references.title: LieART: Lie Algebras and Representation Theory
references.authors: Robert Feger, Thomas W. Kephart, Robert J. Saskowski, and contributors
references.summary: Official Wolfram Language paclet implementing LieART 2.0 calculations, with package code, Mathematica documentation, representation-property tables, tensor products, and branching rules.
references.project_relevance: The executable counterpart of the LieART 2.0 paper, suitable for reproducible checks of SU(N) irreps and decomposition channels while the project designs a non-Abelian herald model.

references.title: Quantum Spin Liquids
references.authors: Lucile Savary, Leon Balents
references.summary: Review of quantum spin liquids, their long-range entanglement, fractionalized excitations, emergent gauge theories, parton descriptions, and experimental probes.
references.project_relevance: Broad condensed-matter motivation for why a symmetry-enriched topological-code model may be physically meaningful; it does not specify the project's herald observation or decoder.

references.title: Classifying Fractionalization: Symmetry Classification of Gapped Z2 Spin Liquids in Two Dimensions
references.authors: Andrew M. Essin, Michael Hermele
references.summary: Classifies symmetry fractionalization in gapped two-dimensional Z2 spin liquids, including time-reversal and SO(3) spin-rotation symmetry, using projective representations carried by anyons.
references.project_relevance: Direct background for distinguishing an SU(2)/SO(3)-enriched anyon model from an ordinary toric code without claiming a decoder mechanism.

references.title: Classification of Symmetry Fractionalization in Gapped Z2 Spin Liquids
references.authors: Yang Qi, Meng Cheng
references.summary: Derives constraints on symmetry fractionalization of spinons in gapped Z2 spin liquids with an odd number of spin-1/2 moments per unit cell and classifies symmetric kagome and triangular-lattice cases.
references.project_relevance: Provides a precise physical route by which spinon excitations can carry half-integer spin, while leaving the project's measurable-herald model open.

references.title: Measuring Space-Group Symmetry Fractionalization in Z2 Spin Liquids
references.authors: Michael Zaletel, Yuan-Ming Lu, Ashvin Vishwanath
references.summary: Connects SET invariants to physical observables in Z2 spin liquids with SU(2) spin-rotation invariance, with a kagome-cylinder construction.
references.project_relevance: Useful motivation for separating an abstract symmetry label from an operationally accessible observable in any future non-Abelian herald model.

references.title: Symmetry Fractionalization, Defects, and Gauging of Topological Phases
references.authors: Maissam Barkeshli, Parsa Bonderson, Meng Cheng, Zhenghan Wang
references.summary: Develops a general framework for symmetry fractionalization, symmetry defects, and gauging in 2+1-dimensional topological phases, including non-Abelian anyons and symmetry actions that permute quasiparticle types.
references.project_relevance: The general SET reference for keeping ordinary representation tensor products distinct from anyonic fusion and categorical data.

references.title: Quantum Spin Liquid States
references.authors: Yi Zhou, Kazushi Kanoda, Tai-Kai Ng
references.summary: Introductory review of spin-1/2 quantum spin liquids, including SU(2), U(1), and Z2 parton descriptions, tensor-network approaches, Kitaev models, and material contexts.
references.project_relevance: A complementary condensed-matter and pedagogical background source for future physical motivation, not a proposed implementation target.

references.title: Quantum Computing with Anyons Is Fault Tolerant
references.authors: Anasuya Lyons, Benjamin J. Brown
references.summary: Presents a fault-tolerant scheme for universal anyonic computation with noisy circuit elements, using repeated measurements, a just-in-time decoder, and gauging/ungauging operations in a D(S3) quantum double.
references.project_relevance: A direct reference for extending a herald decoder beyond a static snapshot: measurement error requires a time-resolved syndrome-herald model and a decoder that can defer uncertain corrections.

references.title: Intrinsic Heralding and Optimal Decoders for Non-Abelian Topological Order
references.authors: Dian Jing, Pablo Sala, Liang Jiang, Ruben Verresen
references.summary: Uses measured intermediate fusion products as intrinsic heralds for active error correction in D4 non-Abelian topological order, deriving conditioned optimal decoding and an intrinsically heralded MWPM decoder under perfect measurements.
references.project_relevance: The closest direct literature precedent for a decoder that exploits a non-Abelian fusion-derived herald; its D4 model and perfect-measurement setting are a comparison point, not an implementation of this project's SU(2) model.

references.title: Non-Abelian Topological Order and Anyons on a Trapped-Ion Processor
references.authors: Mohsin Iqbal, Nathanan Tantivasadakarn, Ruben Verresen, Sara L. Campbell, Joan M. Dreiling, Caroline Figgatt, John P. Gaebler, Jacob Johansen, Michael Mills, Steven A. Moses, Juan M. Pino, Anthony Ransford, Mary Rowe, Peter Siegfried, Russell P. Stutz, Michael Foss-Feig, Ashvin Vishwanath, Henrik Dreyer
references.summary: Prepares D4 non-Abelian topological order on a 27-qubit trapped-ion kagome lattice and demonstrates non-Abelian anyon control and Borromean-ring interferometry.
references.project_relevance: Provides the concrete D4 topological-order realization underlying the intrinsic-heralding decoder example, while remaining separate from an active-error-correction demonstration.

references.title: Integer Linear Programming Decoder for Abelian and Non-Abelian Topological Codes
references.authors: Dian Jing, Aubrey Zhang, Liang Jiang, Ruben Verresen
references.summary: Introduces an ILP decoder for general Abelian and non-Abelian topological orders, encoding fusion rules as linear constraints; it includes a spacetime measurement-error formulation and proposes a just-in-time continuous-decoding variant.
references.project_relevance: The most direct current reference for a measurement-noise-aware D4 intrinsic-heralding decoder: it supplies an ILP formulation and a just-in-time protocol, but leaves their continuous-decoding numerical study and threshold proof open.

references.title: PyMatching Decoder
references.authors: Oscar Higgott, Craig Gidney, and contributors
references.summary: Official Python/C++ implementation of sparse-blossom MWPM, including weighted boundaries and correlated matching.
references.project_relevance: The maintained matching back end used by Lab 001 and by the archived BeliefMatching implementation.

references.title: Fermionic Magnons, Non-Abelian Spinons, and Spin Quantum Hall Effect from an Exactly Solvable Kitaev Model with SU(2) Symmetry
references.authors: Hong Yao, Dung-Hai Lee
references.summary: Constructs an exactly solvable spin-1/2 model on the decorated honeycomb lattice with global SU(2) symmetry. When time-reversal symmetry is broken, its deconfined vortices bind spin-1/2 and obey non-Abelian statistics.
references.project_relevance: A concrete microscopic example in which global SU(2) symmetry protects spinful non-Abelian vortex excitations. It motivates, but does not specify, the project's representation-resolved measurement record, herald likelihood, or decoder.

references.title: Stability and Loop Models from Decohering Non-Abelian Topological Order
references.authors: Pablo Sala, Ruben Verresen
references.summary: Maps specified channels that proliferate non-Abelian anyons to loop models with a topological loop weight fixed by the anyon quantum dimension. It relates logical-state fidelity at maximal decoherence to random loop and spin models, and gives quantum-double and Kitaev-honeycomb examples.
references.project_relevance: Provides a source-backed statistical-mechanics background for deriving a noise-channel-specific recoverability transition in non-Abelian topological memory. It does not specify the project's SU(N) representation-resolved herald observation, decoder likelihood, or a decoder threshold.
